meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'just'.
Secondary conversational sense ('easy') (это просто = it's easy) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'horror, terror' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: What on earth is this horror?

examples.text: Что это за ужас такой? И когда это было?
examples.trans: What on earth is this horror? And when was this?

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'равиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to get poisoned', paired with 'отравляться'.

examples.text: Главное, чтобы другие гости не отравились.
examples.trans: The main thing is that other guests do not get poisoned.
Could she really have gotten poisoned by our food?

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: genitive also 'коньяку' (some cognac)

examples.trans: And you're drinking French cognac yourself.

meanings.note: + prepositional; об before a vowel: об этом

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
Secondary conversational sense ('there isn't') (+ genitive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('that') (conjunction) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = well?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'сделать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to make') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Hi, Arkady Borisovich. What are you doing?

meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to give', forming an aspectual pair with 'давать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Derived feminine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'bottle'.

examples.trans: With a bottle of wine in your hand?

examples.text: Пыталась? С бутылкой вина в руке?
examples.trans: You tried? With a bottle of wine in your hand?

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('that') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
in 'то, что ...' = 'what, the thing that'
joins a description to a noun; agrees with that noun in gender and number

examples.trans: This is a mayor who keeps his word.
Where is the book that was here?

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: the infinitive 'Стоять!' as a police order
the infinitive 'Стоять!' as a police order

examples.text: То есть просто стоять и смотреть?
examples.trans: So we just stand and watch?

examples.text: Стоять на месте, никто не выходит из кухни без разрешения!
examples.trans: Freeze right there, nobody leaves the kitchen without permission!

справа.gloss: on the right, to the right

meanings.en: on the right, to the right
meanings.note: справа от + genitive = to the right of

examples.trans: There to the right of the door!
The shop is located to the right of the entrance.

examples.text: Как не нашла? Послушай, в чёрном шкафу посмотри. Там справа от двери!
examples.trans: What do you mean you didn't find it? Listen, look in the black cabinet. There to the right of the door!

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('here') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('! = you'll see!') (emphasis) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('other, another, different').
Secondary conversational sense ('different') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Послушайте, а можно в другое место? Здесь плохо пахнет.
examples.trans: Listen, could we go somewhere else? It smells bad in here.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Secondary conversational sense ('? = really?, oh yeah?') (disbelief) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

забрать.gloss: to take back, to take away

meanings.en: to take away, to pick up
meanings.note: забрать заявление = to withdraw a statement
забрать заявление = to withdraw a statement

examples.text: Поговори с Аракеляном. Пусть он заберёт заявление.
examples.trans: Talk to Arakelyan. Get him to withdraw his statement.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'it is necessary'.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'ago'.
Secondary conversational sense ('back, backwards') (шаг назад = a step back) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я их ещё два года назад им выделил!
examples.trans: I allocated it to them two years ago!

examples.text: Я их ещё два года назад им выделил! Я сам приказ подписывал!
examples.trans: I allocated it to them two years ago! I signed the order myself!

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'can', forming an aspectual pair with 'смочь'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'to' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)

meanings.en: to come up to, to approach
meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ойти'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to come up', forming an aspectual pair with 'подходить'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to suit, to fit') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Нам не нужна ваша приставка! Ещё раз подойдёте к моему ребёнку — пожалеете!
examples.trans: We don't need your console! Come near my child again and you'll be sorry!

meanings.note: давай + 1st person plural or infinitive
давай + 1st person plural or infinitive

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: + infinitive; agrees with the subject: должна (f)
Secondary conversational sense ('owe') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Жадность, Паша, должна быть умеренная. Комнатной температуры.
examples.trans: Greed, Pasha, should be moderate. Room temperature.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'clear'.
Secondary conversational sense ('I see') (as a reply) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm going to be mayor, understood?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'next'.
Secondary conversational sense ('next, go on') (in a list or a story) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: А дальше? Я очень волнуюсь, я к этому не приспособлена.
examples.trans: And then what? I'm very nervous, I'm not cut out for this.
